polity.en: English Crown, then East India Company (from 1668)
polity.zh: 英国王室，1668年起东印度公司

summary.en: Seven islands ceded by Gujarat to Portugal in 1534 passed to England as part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry in 1661. Reclaimed and joined, they grew into Bombay, India’s great port and financial capital, officially renamed Mumbai in 1995.
summary.zh: 这七个岛屿于1534年由古吉拉特割让给葡萄牙，1661年作为凯瑟琳公主的嫁妆转归英国。经填海连成一体后发展为孟买，成为印度最大的港口和金融中心，1995年正式更名为Mumbai。

sources.title: Mariam Dossal, Theatre of Conflict, City of Hope: Mumbai 1660 to Present Times (2010)

name.zh: 马德拉斯帕特南／马德拉斯（圣乔治堡）

summary.en: The East India Company acquired a coastal strip from a Vijayanagara nayaka in 1639 and built Fort St George, around which Madras grew as capital of the Madras Presidency. The city was renamed Chennai, after the neighbouring town of Chennapatnam, in 1996.
summary.zh: 东印度公司于1639年从毗奢耶那伽罗属下的纳亚克手中取得一段海岸并修建圣乔治堡，马德拉斯围绕该堡发展为马德拉斯管区首府。1996年依邻近的金奈帕特南之名改称金奈。

name.zh: 加尔各答（卡利卡塔、苏塔努蒂、戈宾德布尔）

polity.en: East India Company (capital of British India)
polity.zh: 东印度公司（英属印度首府）

summary.en: Job Charnock’s East India Company post of 1690 on the Hooghly absorbed three villages and became Calcutta, capital of British India until 1911 and centre of the Bengal Renaissance. Its Bengali name Kolkata became official in 2001.
summary.zh: 1690年约伯·查诺克在胡格利河畔设立东印度公司商站，合并三个村落形成加尔各答；该城至1911年一直是英属印度首府，也是孟加拉文艺复兴的中心。2001年正式采用孟加拉语名称Kolkata。

sources.title: P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (1987)

polity.zh: 托马拉王朝与乔汉王朝

summary.en: Traditionally identified with the epic Indraprastha, Delhi has been rebuilt as a succession of cities: Tomara Dhillika, the sultanate capitals, Shah Jahan’s Shahjahanabad and Lutyens’s New Delhi, capital of British India from 1911 and of the Republic of India.
summary.zh: 德里传统上被认为即史诗中的因陀罗普拉斯塔，历史上曾多次重建为不同城市：托马拉王朝的迪利卡、苏丹国诸都城、沙贾汗的沙贾汉纳巴德以及勒琴斯设计的新德里；1911年起为英属印度首都，后为印度共和国首都。

sources.title: Narayani Gupta, Delhi Between Two Empires 1803–1931 (1981)
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)

note: The Tomara founding (traditionally 736) is uncertain; Indraprastha is legendary and is not given a date range. Shahjahanabad was built 1639–1648.

polity.en: Pala Empire and later Bihar rulers
polity.zh: 波罗王朝及其后比哈尔诸政权
苏尔王朝，后为莫卧儿帝国
莫卧儿帝国／孟加拉纳瓦卜

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Pataliputra on the Ganges was the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires and the city where Aryabhata worked. Lying in ruins by Xuanzang’s visit, it was refounded as Patna by Sher Shah Suri in 1541 and is now capital of Bihar.
summary.zh: 恒河畔的华氏城曾是孔雀王朝和笈多王朝的都城，阿耶波多亦在此著述。玄奘到访时已成废墟，1541年舍尔沙·苏尔在此重建巴特那，今为比哈尔邦首府。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)

note: Polity labels before 320 and for 550–1541 are simplified; the Azimabad name (after prince Azim-us-Shan) was used alongside Patna.

polity.zh: 杜兰尼帝国／锡克米斯尔

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Capital of the later Ghaznavids, a Mughal imperial city adorned with the fort and Badshahi Mosque, and seat of Ranjit Singh’s Sikh Empire, Lahore became the capital of Punjab under the British and is Pakistan’s second-largest city.
summary.zh: 拉合尔曾是后期伽色尼王朝的都城、莫卧儿帝国的重要城市（建有拉合尔堡和巴德沙希清真寺），又为兰吉特·辛格锡克帝国的都城；英治时期为旁遮普首府，今为巴基斯坦第二大城市。

sources.title: Anna Suvorova, Lahore: Topophilia of Space and Place (2011)

name.zh: 伊拉哈巴斯／阿拉哈巴德

summary.en: Prayaga, at the sacred confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna, hosted Harsha’s alms-giving assemblies and the Kumbh Mela. Akbar built a fort here and named it Ilahabas (1575), later Allahabad; the old name Prayagraj was restored in 2018.
summary.zh: 钵逻耶伽位于恒河与亚穆纳河的神圣交汇处，戒日王曾在此举行布施大会，也是大壶节举办地。阿克巴于1575年在此筑堡并命名为伊拉哈巴斯，后称阿拉哈巴德；2018年恢复古名普拉亚格拉杰。

sources.title: Abu'l-Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari (tr. H. S. Jarrett), Subah of Ilahabad

note: Akbar’s foundation is dated 1575 in most accounts, 1583 in some.

polity.en: Ghurids, then Delhi Sultanate and Jaunpur
polity.zh: 古尔王朝，后为德里苏丹国与焦恩布尔

summary.en: One of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, Kashi on the Ganges is Hinduism’s holiest city and lies near Sarnath, where the Buddha first preached. Known to the British as Benares, it officially became Varanasi in 1956.
summary.zh: 迦尸位于恒河畔，是世界上最古老的持续有人居住的城市之一，也是印度教最神圣的城市，邻近佛陀初转法轮的鹿野苑。英国人称之为贝拿勒斯，1956年正式定名瓦拉纳西。

sources.title: Diana L. Eck, Banaras: City of Light (1982)

note: Early polity labels omitted; date of the Benares State’s founding (1737) follows conventional accounts.

summary.en: A harbour known to Arab traders (Ibn Battuta called it Kalanpu in 1344), Colombo was fortified by the Portuguese, made the Dutch and then British capital of Ceylon, and remains Sri Lanka’s commercial capital beside the administrative capital Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
summary.zh: 科伦坡早为阿拉伯商人所知（伊本·白图泰1344年称之为卡兰普），后由葡萄牙人筑城，相继成为荷兰与英国统治下锡兰的首府；今为斯里兰卡的商业首都，行政首都为毗邻的斯里贾亚瓦德纳普拉科特。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)
Ibn Battuta, Rihla (tr. H. A. R. Gibb)

note: The first name range starts at Ibn Battuta’s mention; the port is older. Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte became the official (legislative) capital in 1982; Colombo remains the executive and commercial capital.

polity.zh: 莫卧儿帝国（孟加拉省首府）

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度
巴基斯坦（东巴基斯坦首府）

summary.en: Made the Mughal capital of Bengal by Islam Khan in 1610 and named Jahangirnagar after the emperor, Dhaka was famed for its muslin. It was capital of East Bengal and East Pakistan and, since 1971, of Bangladesh; the spelling Dhaka replaced Dacca in 1982.
summary.zh: 1610年伊斯兰汗将达卡定为莫卧儿孟加拉省首府，并以皇帝之名称为贾汉吉尔纳加尔，此地以细棉布闻名。后为东孟加拉和东巴基斯坦首府，1971年起为孟加拉国首都；1982年拼写由Dacca改为Dhaka。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204–1760 (1993)

note: Dhaka is first securely attested in a mosque inscription of 1459; Islam Khan’s move is dated 1608 or 1610 in different sources.

name.zh: 科利格拉马（扬布与扬加拉聚落）

polity.en: Licchavi and Thakuri kings of Nepal
polity.zh: 尼泊尔李查维及塔库里诸王
马拉王国（都于巴克塔普尔）
尼泊尔联邦民主共和国

summary.en: The largest city of the Himalayan valley, a Newar trading town of temples and courtyards. The name comes from the Kasthamandap, a wooden pavilion said to be built from a single tree; Prithvi Narayan Shah made it the capital of unified Nepal in 1768.
summary.zh: 喜马拉雅谷地最大的城市，原是遍布神庙与庭院的尼瓦尔商业城镇。城名源于相传由一棵树木建成的木构亭阁“卡斯塔曼达普”；1768年普里特维·纳拉扬·沙阿以其为统一后的尼泊尔首都。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Kathmandu Valley

note: Licchavi-era names come from inscriptions; the name Kathmandu is attested from about the 16th century.

polity.zh: 毗奢耶那伽罗附庸肯佩·高达
比贾布尔苏丹国（沙哈吉·蓬斯勒的封地）
英国宗主权下的迈索尔（1831年起为首府）
印度（迈索尔邦 / 卡纳塔克邦首府）

summary.en: Founded with a mud fort by the chieftain Kempe Gowda in 1537, sold to Mysore in 1689 and turned into a British cantonment after Tipu Sultan’s fall. Its science institutes and later its software industry made it India’s technology capital; the Kannada form Bengaluru became official in 2014.
summary.zh: 1537年由酋长肯佩·高达筑土堡建城，1689年被售予迈索尔，蒂普苏丹败亡后成为英国兵站。科研机构和后来的软件产业使其成为印度的科技之都；2014年正式采用卡纳达语名称Bengaluru。

sources.title: Janaki Nair, The Promise of the Metropolis: Bangalore’s Twentieth Century (2005)

polity.zh: 甘波拉王国，后为科特王国

name.zh: 森卡达加拉普拉 / 坎达乌达拉塔（康提）

summary.en: The hill capital of the last Sinhalese kingdom, built around a lake and the Temple of the Tooth. Europeans named it from the Sinhala Kanda Uda Rata, “the land on the mountain”; the British took it in 1815 and it remains Sri Lanka’s cultural and Buddhist centre.
summary.zh: 最后一个僧伽罗王国的山地都城，环湖而建，城中有佛牙寺。欧洲人根据僧伽罗语“坎达乌达拉塔”（山上之地）称之为康提；1815年英国占领此城，至今仍是斯里兰卡的文化与佛教中心。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sacred City of Kandy
K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (rev. 2005)

note: Founding by Vikramabahu III of Gampola (c. 1357–1374) follows the Sinhalese chronicles.

name.zh: 阿努拉德普勒（圣城遗址）

polity.zh: 僧伽罗诸王国与万尼酋长

summary.en: Capital of Sri Lanka for over a millennium and one of the great cities of ancient Asia, with stupas second only to the Egyptian pyramids in bulk and the Sri Maha Bodhi, a fig tree grown from a cutting of the Buddha’s tree. After the Chola sack of 1017 the jungle closed over it until restoration in the 19th century.
summary.zh: 斯里兰卡逾千年的都城，古代亚洲的大城之一，其佛塔体量仅次于埃及金字塔；城中的“室利摩诃菩提树”据说由佛陀菩提树的枝条培育而成。1017年朱罗人洗劫后，城市被丛林掩没，直到19世纪才重新修复。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sacred City of Anuradhapura
Robin Coningham, Anuradhapura: The British–Sri Lankan Excavations at Anuradhapura Salgaha Watta 2 (1999–2006)

note: Founded by tradition in 377 BCE; the first entry starts at the atlas floor of 50 BCE.

name.zh: 阿沙瓦尔 / 卡尔纳瓦蒂

polity.zh: 遮娄其（索兰基）与瓦格拉诸王

name.zh: 阿沙瓦尔 / 卡尔纳瓦蒂

polity.zh: 德里苏丹国，1407年起古吉拉特苏丹国
马拉塔佩什瓦与盖克瓦德家族

summary.en: Founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmad Shah I beside the older town of Ashaval/Karnavati on the Sabarmati. Its Indo-Islamic mosques and pol neighbourhoods made it India’s first UNESCO World Heritage City; textile mills earned it the name “Manchester of the East”, and Gandhi’s ashram stood on its riverbank.
summary.zh: 1411年由苏丹艾哈迈德·沙一世在萨巴尔马蒂河畔、旧城阿沙瓦尔/卡尔纳瓦蒂旁建立。其印度-伊斯兰风格清真寺和“波尔”街区使它成为印度第一座世界遗产城市；纺织厂为它赢得“东方曼彻斯特”之称，甘地的修道院就坐落在河岸上。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic City of Ahmadabad
Kenneth L. Gillion, Ahmedabad: A Study in Indian Urban History (1968)

note: Karnavati is traditionally ascribed to the Chaulukya king Karna (r. c. 1064–1092); its exact site relative to Ashaval is debated.

polity.en: Kingdom of Mrauk U (Arakan), with Portuguese settlers
polity.zh: 阿拉干妙乌王国（有葡萄牙定居者）

polity.en: East India Company, then British India
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度
巴基斯坦（东孟加拉 / 东巴基斯坦）

summary.en: Bangladesh’s great seaport at the mouth of the Karnaphuli river. Contested between Bengal and Arakan, it was a base of Portuguese adventurers until the Mughal governor Shaista Khan captured it in 1666 and renamed it Islamabad. The government adopted the Bengali spelling Chattogram in 2018.
summary.zh: 孟加拉国位于卡纳普利河口的大海港。它曾在孟加拉与阿拉干之间几度易手，是葡萄牙冒险者的据点，直到1666年莫卧儿总督沙伊斯塔汗攻占此城并更名为伊斯兰堡。2018年政府采用孟加拉语拼法Chattogram。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier (1993)

note: Control alternated between Bengal, Tripura and Arakan in the 15th–16th centuries; 1459 marks the beginning of Arakanese claims and is approximate.

polity.en: Rashtrakutas, Yadavas, then the Deccan sultanates
polity.zh: 罗湿陀罗拘陀、亚达瓦，后为德干诸苏丹国
蓬斯勒家族封地；1674年起属马拉塔王国
马拉塔联盟（佩什瓦驻地）

summary.en: A small town in Shahaji Bhonsle’s jagir where the young Shivaji grew up, then the seat of the Peshwas, who ruled the Maratha Confederacy from its Shaniwar Wada palace. Under the British it became a monsoon capital and a centre of reformers such as Jyotirao Phule and Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
summary.zh: 原是沙哈吉·蓬斯勒封地内的小镇，少年西瓦吉在此长大；后成为佩什瓦驻地，他们在沙尼瓦尔瓦达宫统治马拉塔联盟。英治时期它是雨季首府，也是乔蒂劳·普勒、巴尔·甘加达尔·提拉克等改革家的活动中心。

sources.title: Stewart Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (New Cambridge History of India II.4, 1993)

note: The earliest mention is “Punnaka” in a Rashtrakuta copper plate of 758. The Peshwas made Pune their seat from 1749.

polity.zh: 印度-斯基泰与印度-帕提亚诸王

polity.en: Kidarites, Hephthalites, then the Turk and Hindu Shahis
polity.zh: 寄多罗、嚈哒，后为突厥沙希与印度沙希

name.zh: 帕拉沙瓦尔 / 巴尔沙瓦尔

polity.zh: 伽色尼、古尔及后来的苏丹国

polity.en: Durrani Empire (winter capital) and Barakzai chiefs
polity.zh: 杜兰尼帝国（冬都）及巴拉克宰酋长

summary.en: The gateway city below the Khyber Pass. As Purushapura it was Kanishka’s capital, with a great stupa that Faxian and Xuanzang admired; the name Peshawar, often explained as “frontier town”, is linked to the Mughal emperor Akbar.
summary.zh: 开伯尔山口下的门户城市。作为布路沙布逻，它曾是迦腻色伽的都城，城中大塔令法显与玄奘赞叹；“白沙瓦”一名常被解释为“边城”，与莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴有关。

sources.title: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji, book 2 (Gandhara)
Ahmad Hasan Dani, Peshawar: Historic City of the Frontier (1969)

note: The date the name Peshawar came into use is uncertain; Akbar-era sources use it, while al-Biruni (11th c.) writes Purshawar.

polity.en: Kingdom of Mysore (Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan)
polity.zh: 迈索尔王国（海德尔·阿里与蒂普苏丹）

summary.en: The pepper port of the Zamorin kings, visited by Ibn Battuta and by Zheng He’s fleets and reached by Vasco da Gama in 1498. Its fine cotton cloth gave English the word “calico”.
summary.zh: 扎莫林国王的胡椒港，伊本·白图泰和郑和船队都曾到访，1498年瓦斯科·达伽马也抵达此地。这里出产的细棉布为英语贡献了“calico”（白棉布）一词。

sources.title: K. V. Krishna Ayyar, The Zamorins of Calicut (1938)
Ma Huan, Yingya Shenglan (1433), tr. J. V. G. Mills (1970)

note: The rise of the Zamorins as rulers of Calicut is dated variously to the 12th–13th centuries.

name.zh: 蒂鲁瓦南塔普拉姆（斯亚南杜拉普拉姆）
蒂鲁瓦南塔普拉姆（特里凡得琅）

polity.zh: 特拉凡科尔-科钦邦（印度）

name.zh: 特里凡得琅（蒂鲁瓦南塔普拉姆）

summary.en: The city of the Padmanabhaswamy temple, “the city of the sacred serpent Ananta”. Travancore’s rulers moved their capital here in 1795 and dedicated their kingdom to the temple deity. The official name returned from Trivandrum to Thiruvananthapuram in 1991.
summary.zh: 帕德马纳巴斯瓦米神庙所在地，意为“圣蛇阿难陀之城”。特拉凡科尔王室于1795年迁都于此，并把王国献给神庙主神。1991年官方名称由Trivandrum改回Thiruvananthapuram。

sources.title: A. Sreedhara Menon, A Survey of Kerala History (1967)

note: The Venad-era start date is approximate.

name.zh: 海得拉巴（相传又名巴格纳加尔）

polity.zh: 戈尔康达苏丹国（库特布·沙希王朝）
海得拉巴土邦（都于奥兰加巴德）
海得拉巴土邦（阿萨夫·贾希尼扎姆）

polity.en: India (capital of Hyderabad State, then Andhra Pradesh)
polity.zh: 印度（海得拉巴邦、后安得拉邦首府）

summary.en: Laid out in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah around the Charminar as a new capital beside crowded Golconda. Seat of the Nizams, the richest princely rulers in India, it later grew into a centre of pharmaceuticals and software.
summary.zh: 1591年穆罕默德·库利·库特布·沙以查尔米纳尔为中心规划建设，作为拥挤的戈尔康达旁的新都。它是印度最富有的土邦君主尼扎姆的驻地，后来发展为制药和软件产业中心。

note: The story that the city was first named Bhagnagar after a dancer, Bhagmati, is a later tradition.

polity.zh: 帕拉瓦治下的穆塔赖亚尔酋长

polity.en: Chola dynasty (capital moved to Gangaikonda Cholapuram)
polity.zh: 朱罗王朝（迁都恒河征服者朱罗城）
潘地亚、马杜赖苏丹国，后为毗奢耶那伽罗
英属印度（马德拉斯管区）

summary.en: The Chola capital on the Kaveri delta, crowned by Rajaraja I’s Brihadisvara temple. Later Nayak and Maratha kings made it a centre of Carnatic music, Bharatanatyam and Tanjore painting; the British annexed the kingdom in 1855 under the doctrine of lapse.
summary.zh: 高韦里河三角洲上的朱罗都城，以罗阇罗阇一世建造的布里哈迪希瓦拉神庙为标志。后来的纳亚克和马拉塔国王使其成为卡纳提克音乐、婆罗多舞和坦焦尔绘画的中心；1855年英国依据“无嗣失权”原则吞并该王国。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḷas (1955)
V. Vriddhagirisan, The Nayaks of Tanjore (1942)

note: Vijayalaya Chola took Thanjavur c. 850 from the Mutharaiyars.
